قرب_1.why: قَرِبَ يَقْرَبُ (to come near). Every Quranic present is a prohibition in the jussive (لَا تَقْرَبَا, 2:35; لَا تَقْرَبُوا), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَقْرَبُ.

جيأ_1.why: جَاءَ يَجِيءُ (to come). The Quran uses it only in the past; the hollow-yāʾ present يَجِيءُ is standard.

مسس_1.why: مَسَّ (مَسِسَ) يَمَسُّ (to touch). The Quran's presents all carry object pronouns or are subjunctive/jussive (لَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي, 3:47 — the fatḥa shows the vowel), which the fit cannot read.

ترك_1.why: تَرَكَ يَتْرُكُ (to leave). Its active presents are only subjunctive/jussive (تَتْرُكْ, 7:176), which the fit cannot read; the attested imperative ٱتْرُكِ (44:24) shows the ḍamma.

ردد_1.why: رَدَّ يَرُدُّ (to return, send back). Its Quranic presents carry clitics or mood endings the fit cannot read; يَرُدُّ is standard.

كفي_1.why: كَفَى يَكْفِي (to suffice). Its Quranic presents carry object pronouns (يَكْفِيَكُمْ), which the fit cannot read; يَكْفِي is standard.

سوأ_1.why: سَاءَ يَسُوءُ (to be evil, to grieve). Its Quranic presents carry clitics or mood endings the fit cannot read; يَسُوءُ is standard.

خلو_1.why: خَلَا يَخْلُو (to pass away, be alone). The Quran's presents carry clitics or mood endings the fit cannot read; يَخْلُو is standard.

أذن_1.why: أَذِنَ يَأْذَنُ (to permit). Its presents are only subjunctive/jussive or passive (ءَاذَنَ, 7:123), which the fit cannot read; the imperative ٱئْذَن (9:49) shows the fatḥa.

فتن_1.why: فَتَنَ يَفْتِنُ (to try, tempt). Its Quranic presents carry clitics or mood endings the fit cannot read; يَفْتِنُ is standard.

حقق_1.why: حَقَّ يَحِقُّ (to be due, come true). Its Quranic presents carry clitics or mood endings the fit cannot read; يَحِقُّ is standard.

وقي_1.why: وَقَى يَقِي (to guard). Its Quranic presents carry clitics or mood endings the fit cannot read (the imperative قُوٓا۟ 66:6 cannot show the vowel); يَقِي is standard.

صدق_1.why: صَدَقَ يَصْدُقُ (to be truthful). The Quran uses it only in the past; يَصْدُقُ is standard.

غرر_1.why: غَرَّ يَغُرُّ (to delude). Its Quranic presents are jussive with clitics (لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ, 3:196), which the fit cannot read; يَغُرُّ is standard.

بدأ_1.why: بَدَأَ يَبْدَأُ (to begin). The Quran writes the present with the Uthmani seat يَبْدَؤُا۟ (10:4) — the fatḥa shows the vowel, but the fit cannot read the spelling.

حبط_1.why: حَبِطَ يَحْبَطُ (to come to nothing). Its Quranic presents are in mood forms with clitics the fit cannot read; يَحْبَطُ is standard.

وقع_1.why: وَقَعَ يَقَعُ (to fall, happen). Its only present is subjunctive (أَنْ تَقَعَ, 22:65 — the fatḥa shows the vowel), which the fit cannot read.

بدو_1.why: بَدَا يَبْدُو (to appear). The Quran has it in the past and only a passive jussive present (تُبْدَ, 5:101); يَبْدُو is standard.

عرض_1.why: عَرَضَ يَعْرِضُ (to present, show). The Quran has it only in the past and passive; يَعْرِضُ is standard.

هود_1.why: هَادَ يَهُودُ (to be a Jew; to return in repentance). The Quran has it only in the past (هَادُوا, هُدْنَا 7:156); يَهُودُ is standard.

فطر_1.why: فَطَرَ يَفْطُرُ (to originate, create; to split). Its only Quranic presents are the Form V يَتَفَطَّرْنَ, filed under Form I (see corpus_corrections), so nothing is left to fit; يَفْطُرُ is standard.

نبذ_1.why: نَبَذَ يَنْبِذُ (to cast aside). Its only active forms are past or imperative (ٱنۢبِذْ, 8:58 — the kasra shows the vowel); the one present is passive (لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ, 104:4), which the fit cannot read.

تبع_1.why: تَبِعَ يَتْبَعُ (to follow). Its Quranic presents carry clitics (يَتْبَعُهَآ, 2:263), which the fit cannot read; يَتْبَعُ is standard.

فرض_1.why: فَرَضَ يَفْرِضُ (to make obligatory, to assign). The Quran uses it only in the past (فَرَضَ, فَرَضْنَا, فَرَضْتُمْ); the dictionaries give يَفْرِضُ.

خسف_1.why: خَسَفَ يَخْسِفُ (to make the earth swallow, to sink). The Quran's presents are jussive or subjunctive with an object (نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ, 34:9; أَن يَخْسِفَ, 16:45), which the fit does not read; the kasra there and the dictionaries give يَخْسِفُ.

نفر_1.why: نَفَرَ يَنْفِرُ (to go forth, to set out). The Quran's presents are jussive or subjunctive (إِلَّا تَنفِرُوا, 9:39; لِيَنفِرُوا, 9:122), which the fit does not read; the kasra there and the dictionaries give يَنْفِرُ.

همم_1.why: هَمَّ يَهُمُّ (to intend, to be about to). The Quran uses it only in the past (هَمَّ, هَمَّتْ, هَمُّوا); the dictionaries give يَهُمُّ, as for doubled faʿala verbs generally.

حضر_1.why: حَضَرَ يَحْضُرُ (to be present, to attend, to come). The Quran's only present carries a suffix (أَن يَحْضُرُونِ, 23:98), which the fit does not read; the ḍamma there and the dictionaries give يَحْضُرُ.

دلل_1.why: دَلَّ يَدُلُّ (to show the way, to point to). Every Quranic present carries an object pronoun (أَدُلُّكُمْ 61:10, نَدُلُّكُمْ 34:7), which the fit cannot read; the doubled verb's present is يَدُلُّ.

دوم_1.why: دَامَ يَدُومُ (to last, to remain). The Quran uses it only in the past (مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا, 19:31); the hollow-wāw present is يَدُومُ.

ثقف_1.why: ثَقِفَ يَثْقَفُ (to come upon, to overtake; to grasp quickly). The Quran's presents are jussive or energic with object pronouns (يَثْقَفُوكُمْ 60:2, تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ 8:57), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَثْقَفُ.

صفح_1.why: صَفَحَ يَصْفَحُ (to pardon, to overlook). The Quran's presents are all jussive (وَلْيَصْفَحُوا 24:22, وَتَصْفَحُوا 64:14), which the fit cannot read; the guttural ḥāʾ gives the fatha of يَصْفَحُ.

علو_1.why: عَلَا يَعْلُو (to rise high, to be haughty). The Quran's presents are jussive or subjunctive (أَلَّا تَعْلُوا 27:31), which the fit cannot read; the defective-wāw present is يَعْلُو.

بوأ_1.why: بَاءَ يَبُوءُ (to return with, to incur). The Quran's only present is the subjunctive تَبُوأَ (5:29); the hollow-wāw present is يَبُوءُ.

غضب_1.why: غَضِبَ يَغْضَبُ (to become angry). The Quran uses it only in the past (غَضِبَ, غَضِبُوا); the dictionaries give يَغْضَبُ.

وسع_1.why: وَسِعَ يَسَعُ (to encompass, to have room for). The Quran uses it only in the past (وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ, 2:255); the dictionaries give يَسَعُ, whose wāw drops like يَضَعُ's.

برز_1.why: بَرَزَ يَبْرُزُ (to come out, to appear). The Quran uses it only in the past (بَرَزُوا); the dictionaries give يَبْرُزُ.

ملأ_1.why: مَلَأَ يَمْلَأُ (to fill). The Quran's forms are passive (مُلِئَتْ, 72:8) or carry an emphatic nūn (لَأَمْلَأَنَّ, 7:18 — the fatḥa shows the vowel), which the fit cannot read.

بخس_1.why: بَخَسَ يَبْخَسُ (to cheat of, to diminish). Its Quranic presents are jussive or passive (لَا يَبْخَسْ, 2:282; لَا يُبْخَسُونَ), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَبْخَسُ.

أوي_1.why: أَوَى يَأْوِي (to take shelter). The attested present (سَآوِي, 11:43) is Uthmani with a prefixed future and a hamza seat the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَأْوِي.

جهر_1.why: جَهَرَ يَجْهَرُ (to speak aloud, to make public). The Quran's presents are jussive or carry an object (لَا تَجْهَرْ, 17:110; تَجْهَرُوا, 49:2), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَجْهَرُ.

خون_1.why: خَانَ يَخُونُ (to betray). The Quran's presents are jussive (لَا تَخُونُوا۟, 8:27), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَخُونُ.

دفع_1.why: دَفَعَ يَدْفَعُ (to push, to repel, to hand over). The Quran's forms are imperatives, pasts and a verbal noun (ٱدْفَعْ, فَٱدْفَعُوٓا۟, دَفَعْتُمْ, دَفْعُ), with no plain present the fit can read; the dictionaries give يَدْفَعُ.

ذبح_1.why: ذَبَحَ يَذْبَحُ (to slaughter). The Quran's presents are subjunctive or carry an object pronoun (أَن تَذْبَحُوا۟, 2:67; أَذْبَحُكَ, 37:102), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَذْبَحُ.

رجم_1.why: رَجَمَ يَرْجُمُ (to stone). The Quran's presents carry object pronouns or an emphatic nūn (يَرْجُمُوكُمْ, 18:20; لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ, 19:46), which the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَرْجُمُ.

سلف_1.why: سَلَفَ يَسْلُفُ (to be past, to precede). The Quran uses it only in the past (مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ); the dictionaries give يَسْلُفُ.

شرح_1.why: شَرَحَ يَشْرَحُ (to expand, to open; to explain). The Quran has only the jussive نَشْرَحْ (94:1) and the imperative اِشْرَحْ, which the fit does not use; the dictionaries give يَشْرَحُ.

طعم_1.why: طَعِمَ يَطْعَمُ (to taste, to eat): a kasra past takes a fatha present (cf. 2:249 وَمَن لَّمْ يَطْعَمْهُ).

طمس_1.why: طَمَسَ يَطْمِسُ (to efface, to blot out), cf. 4:47 نَّطْمِسَ and the imperative اِطْمِسْ (10:88).

عتو_1.why: عَتَا يَعْتُو (to be insolent, to rebel). The Quran uses it only in the past (عَتَوْا, عَتَتْ); a final-wāw verb takes a damma present.

عثو_1.why: عَثِيَ يَعْثَى (to act wickedly, to spread corruption), the verb of the Quran's تَعْثَوْا (2:60); the dictionaries give يَعْثَى.

عجل_1.why: عَجِلَ يَعْجَلُ (to hasten, to be in a hurry), cf. 75:16 لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ.

عقر_1.why: عَقَرَ يَعْقِرُ (to hamstring, to slaughter an animal). The Quran uses it only in the past (عَقَرُوا); the dictionaries give يَعْقِرُ.

غلل_1.why: غَلَّ يَغُلُّ (to embezzle, to take by fraud), cf. 3:161 أَن يَغُلَّ.

قرر_1.why: قَرَّ يَقَرُّ (of the eye: to be cooled, to be comforted), cf. 20:40 كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا.

فرق_1.why: فَرَقَ يَفْرُقُ (to separate, to part, to distinguish), cf. the imperative فَافْرُقْ (5:25). The corpus's only present, يَفْرَقُونَ (9:56), is فَرِقَ يَفْرَقُ 'to be afraid' (see data/corpus_corrections.json).

هلك_1.why: هَلَكَ يَهْلِكُ (to perish). The Quran's presents the fit could read are passive or Form IV (يُهْلَكُ, يُهْلِكُ); the dictionaries give يَهْلِكُ.

وهن_1.why: وَهَنَ يَهِنُ (to weaken, to lose heart), an assimilated verb that drops its wāw; the Quran's presents are jussive prohibitions (لَا تَهِنُوا, 3:139) the fit cannot read.

تمم_1.why: تَمَّ يَتِمُّ (to be complete). The Quran uses it only in the past; the dictionaries give يَتِمُّ.

ثقل_1.why: ثَقُلَ يَثْقُلُ (to be heavy), a faʿula verb, whose present always takes u. The Quran uses it only in the past.

خرق_1.why: خَرَقَ يَخْرِقُ (to make a hole, to tear through; also يَخْرُقُ). The Quran's only present, لَنْ تَخْرِقَ (17:37), is a subjunctive the fit cannot read.

خيب_1.why: خَابَ يَخِيبُ (to fail, to be disappointed), a hollow-yāʾ verb. The Quran uses it only in the past.

درأ_1.why: دَرَأَ يَدْرَأُ (to avert, to ward off; the hamza, a throat letter, takes a). The Quran writes its presents with an Uthmani silent alef (يَدْرَءُونَ, يَدْرَؤُا۟) the fit cannot read.

سرق_1.why: سَرَقَ يَسْرِقُ (to steal). The Quran's only present, يَسْرِقْنَ (60:12), has a feminine-plural suffix the fit cannot read; the dictionaries give يَسْرِقُ.

سوم_1.why: سَامَ يَسُومُ (to inflict, to subject someone to), a hollow-wāw verb; the Quran's presents carry object pronouns (يَسُومُونَكُمْ, 2:49) the fit cannot read.

صبب_1.why: صَبَّ يَصُبُّ (to pour). The Quran's only present, يُصَبُّ, is passive; the dictionaries give يَصُبُّ.
